request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:** the change is server-side only; the front end and stored data are untouched.
- **New `rollup` package** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`). The `Rollup` service works out each person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's two totals, the same way the screen does. Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count. A due-total is n/a when the grade has no rate today and no claim has a figure. The sheet's due-total skips n/a people.
- **Before and after every change:** a step right after validation saves the sheet's figures. A second step runs after the change's own audit line and compares the figures again. It writes `ROLLUP … person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…` for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added; a new person always counts as moved. If the sheet totals moved, it then writes one `TOTALS … claimed-total=… due-total=…` line.
- **Covers all eight change endpoints:** add/edit person, statement, add/edit claim, claim status, rate and today. Changing today writes no line of its own, only these lines when figures move. A refused change fails before the comparison step, so it writes nothing.
- **Passing the user along:** each validator now also publishes a small `Actor` (who made the change), so the comparison step can write `by=<user>`.

The spec writes the person field as `person=<name>`, while the request text says `name=<name>`. I followed the spec, since that's what the test checks.
